title: He already heard God… so why is he still asking for another sign?
paragraphs: He already heard God… so why is he still asking for another sign?
Because sometimes… obedience isn’t blocked by rebellion—
but by fear wearing a spiritual mask.
You already know what God said.
And delayed obedience… often hides something deeper.

Afraid of failing.
Afraid of looking foolish.
Afraid that maybe—just maybe—he heard God wrong.
So he asked for a sign.
“God, just give me one more confirmation…”
But sometimes… it’s just fear negotiating with obedience.

Not vaguely.
Not confusingly.
Not partially.
“The LORD turned to him and said, ‘Go in the strength you have… Am I not sending you?’… ‘I will be with you, and you will strike down all the Midianites.’”
This is not just about Gideon.
You know that conviction in your heart?
That area God has been pressing on?

The relationship.
The compromise.
The secret habit.
The step of faith.

Fear of loss.
Fear of discomfort.
Fear of surrender.
Fear that obedience might cost you more than disobedience.
But here’s the truth that cuts deep:

You don’t need more signs.
You need more surrender.
This is what will wreck you.
He meets him… in his weakness.
Because God is not intimidated by your struggle.
He doesn’t intend for you to stay there.
The fleece was not the destination.
Gideon needed signs to believe God was with him.
You have Jesus Christ—the full and final revelation of God.
“In the past God spoke… through the prophets… but in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son.”
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not a fleece wet with dew—
but a Savior covered in blood.
And delayed obedience… is still disobedience.
And He didn’t wait for you to get it right.
He died for you while you were still resisting Him.
You don’t clean yourself up first.
Because the same grace that saves you—
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
So now the question is no longer:
“God, will You show me a sign?”
“Will I trust the sign He already gave?”
Because faith is not the absence of fear.
It’s obedience in spite of it.
Jesus is not asking for perfection.
You’ll need it the next time fear starts talking.
From fear to faith — because Jesus rewrites everything.
